name: Veneto
summary: The banner of the Republic of Venice, adapted: the winged Lion of Saint Mark holding an open gospel and resting on sea, land and mountains, with tails along the fly and a border of the provincial arms.
origin: The flag derives from the banner of the Republic of Venice (697–1797). It was adopted by regional law in 1975; a 1999 law removed the words 'Regione del Veneto'.

symbols.name: Lion of Saint Mark
symbols.description: A winged gold lion with an open book reading 'Pax tibi Marce evangelista meus'.

symbols.name: Sea, land and mountains
symbols.description: The ground under the lion's paws.
symbols.meaning: The Adriatic, the Venetian Plain and the Alps.

facts: The open book means peace; a closed book was traditionally associated with war.
clues: A winged lion with an open book, on a banner with tails.
Its lion is the symbol of an evangelist.
The flag of a former maritime republic.
